input.content: You are atto. (golden test system prompt)

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Run a bash command in the working directory and return its combined stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell (use absolute paths or `cd dir && ...`). Stdin is not connected; do not start interactive programs. Output over about 10k tokens is cut from the middle (the start and end are kept), and the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported. With a shell host and session, timeout is a foreground wait (default 10 seconds, maximum 30): a command still running becomes a background job, and an [atto event] arrives when it exits. Follow it with atto job wait <id> -timeout 10m or the exit event. Without a shell host or session, timeout kills the command instead (default 60 seconds, maximum 30 minutes).

description.description: What this command does, in a few words, shown to the user. E.g. "JIT compile atto.py", "Run unit tests", "Read main.go".

timeout.description: Foreground wait in seconds: default 10, maximum 30. A command still running becomes a background job; use atto job wait or its exit event. Without a shell host or session this is a kill timeout: default 60, maximum 1800.

run_in_background.description: Start a background job and return its id immediately instead of waiting up to timeout. Use for dev servers, watchers and long builds; use atto job wait or its exit event to follow completion.
